title: Worksheet 7: Lists (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: A list is a data structure used to store multiple values together in a single, ordered collection, allowing a programmer to work with a whole group of related items using just one variable name. Unlike a single variable, which can only hold one value at a time, a list can hold many values, and those values can even be different data types mixed together, such as a list containing both strings and integers at the same time, depending on the programming language being used. Lists are especially useful when a program needs to work with a collection of similar items, such as a list of student names, a list of high scores, or a list of items in a player's inventory, since storing them together makes it much easier to search through, sort, or update the entire group at once. Because a list keeps its items in a specific order, a programmer can always predict which value comes first, second, or last, unlike some other data structures that do not guarantee any particular order.

questions.text: According to the paragraph, a list is used to:
questions.correct: Store multiple values together in a single ordered collection
distractors: Store exactly one value at a time
Delete data a program no longer needs

questions.text: According to the paragraph, how does a list differ from a single variable?
questions.correct: A list can hold many values, while a single variable holds only one at a time
distractors: A list can only hold numbers
A single variable can hold more values than a list
A list cannot be given a name

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what can a programmer always predict about a list?
questions.correct: Which value comes first, second, or last, because a list keeps its order
distractors: How much memory each item will use
That every item is the same data type
That the list will never change size

questions.text: A program needs to store the names of every student on a robotics team. Based on the paragraph, why is a list a good choice?
questions.correct: It keeps related items together so they are easier to search, sort, or update at once
distractors: It automatically prevents students from being added later
It converts each name into a number
It stores only the longest name in the group

questions.text: Based on the paragraph, what can you conclude about a data structure that does not guarantee any particular order?
questions.correct: You could not rely on always finding the same item in the same position
distractors: It cannot store more than one value
It is always faster than a list
It can only store text values
